reflection.text:
Unblinded compound: cycloheximide / cyclohexamide - ChEMBL CHEMBL123292, 80S Ribosome inhibitor (INHIBITOR of CHEMBL3987582, 80S Ribosome - Protein Nucleic-Acid Complex) - truth MoA: Protein synthesis. Submitted MoA: Microtubule stabilizers p=0.96 - scored incorrect.

What the data did show:
We measured a real, very large tubulin phenotype. e2 at 5 uM: tub_glcm_contrast z=+42.1, tub_mean z=+25.5, tub_std z=+16.7 (n=427 cells). e3 at 50 uM: contrast z=+55.8, mean z=+43.0, nuc_solidity z=-41.1 (n=376 cells). e7 0.5 uM contrast +9.8 and e8 1.5 uM contrast +23.9, mean +11.9, cell_roundness +11.8 show monotonicity. Dose_response e9/e10 rho=+1.00 for tub_mean and contrast, e11 rho=-1.00 for nuc_solidity over 4 doses, 4 wells. This was not noise: dose-dependent increase in tubulin intensity/texture and loss of nuclear solidity/multinucleation is internally consistent and explains the microscopist call in e5: lower density vs DMSO, 8 observations favoring Microtubule stabilizers/Eg5 inhibitors.

Why it misled:
1. Phenotypic mimicry without mechanistic specificity. Cycloheximide is a eukaryotic translation elongation inhibitor of the 80S ribosome PMID 20118940, PMID 32151059, PMID 7201003. It has no direct tubulin binding. However prolonged protein synthesis block causes cell-cycle arrest, failed cytokinesis, cell rounding and secondary cytoskeletal reorganization that can present as increased tubulin staining / bundling texture in fixed images. Our search e19 PubMed 'protein synthesis inhibition microtubule stabilization multinucleation phenotype' returned 0 hits - there was no literature to support a direct link, which should have been a caution, not confirmation.

2. Atlas bias and hypothesis set misspecification. e4 NSC 2/2 Microtubule stabilizers, k-NN 8/10 stabilizers, 2/10 Protein degradation. e12 NSC 3/4 stabilizers, k-NN 7/10 stabilizers, 2/10 Protein degradation, 1/10 Actin disruptors. The atlas gave high similarity at high doses (review noted 0.91, 0.934, 0.813 at 1.5-50 uM) and essentially 100% at top doses. Protein synthesis was not in the reference atlas as a class, and we never added it to hypothesis_history at step 6 or 13: Microtubule stabilizers 0.92->0.96, Protein degradation 0.02, Eg5 0.03->0.01, Aurora 0.02, Microtubule destabilizers 0.01->0.005, Actin 0.005. The closest hint - 2/10 Protein degradation votes at 0.88-0.90 similarity - was discounted because e2/e3/e5 appeared to contradict it, when in fact Protein degradation was the closest proteostasis proxy available.

3. Acquisition and comparison choices that locked in confirmation bias. list_available_experiments showed 8 doses 0.015-50 uM. We sampled only the tubulin-active window: 0.5, 1.5, 5, 50 uM, one replicate/dose, no low-dose baseline where tubulin fragmentation vs stabilization could be separated, and no orthogonal readout. We then did dose_response only on tubulin/nuclear features e9-e11, which guaranteed a perfect rho=+1.00 with n=4 but tested the wrong hypothesis. We did compare_to_reference_atlas twice and update_hypotheses twice on the same features, inflating confidence from 0.92 to 0.96 without independent evidence.

4. Visual validation was not discriminative. e5 microscopy favoring stabilizers/Eg5 cannot distinguish mitotic arrest from direct microtubule stabilization on morphology alone. The paclitaxel-like reference phenotype PMID 16801540, PMID 20442307, PMID 15548390, PMID 18220732 was used as positive control in the rationale, but we never tested the proposed next experiment - in vitro tubulin polymerization, acetylated tubulin, phospho-H3, live mitosis - that would have shown no direct polymerization.

What should have happened: The huge effect sizes z to +55 and 2.5x intensity gain plus 1.5 uM to 50 uM solidity drop to -41 should have prompted suspicion of toxicity/secondary effect, not high confidence. We should have retained Protein synthesis as hypothesis despite atlas absence, noted that Protein degradation signal was non-zero, and required a translation assay - e.g., puromycin incorporation or 35S-Met - and compared to a reference protein synthesis inhibitor rather than relying on morphology alone.
what_was_right: Measured a real dose-dependent tubulin intensity/texture increase: e2 +42.1 contrast/+25.5 mean at 5 uM to e3 +55.8/+43.0 at 50 uM, e7 +9.8 at 0.5 uM, e8 +23.9/+11.9 at 1.5 uM, e9/e10 rho +1.00
Measured a real nuclear shape defect: e11 rho -1.00, e3 nuc_solidity -41.1, consistent with e5 low density and multinucleation/failed cytokinesis
Atlas comparison correctly identified phenotypic similarity to Microtubule stabilizers in the available reference - morphology does mimic paclitaxel-like stabilization PMID 16801540
what_was_wrong: Attributed secondary cytoskeletal changes from 80S inhibition PMID 20118940, PMID 32151059 to direct tubulin stabilization. e19 literature search found 0 hits for translation inhibition -> microtubule stabilization, warning ignored
Hypothesis set omitted truth class entirely; over-weighted NSC 3/4 and k-NN 7-8/10 stabilizer votes while dismissing 2/10 Protein degradation proxy and 1/10 Actin at low dose e7 0.651 similarity
Inflated certainty 0.92->0.96 on n=4 monotonic wells with one replicate/dose, no low-dose control, no orthogonal polymerization or protein synthesis assay

paclitaxel mechanism is microtubule stabilization contrast for atlas match
microtubule stabilization leads to mitotic arrest

reflection.next_experiment: As proposed but with proper controls: 1) cell-free tubulin polymerization assay +/- compound vs paclitaxel and destabilizer, 2) cellular acetylated tubulin and phospho-H3 time course, 3) direct protein synthesis readout puromycin incorporation to test 80S inhibition. This would have separated phenotypic mimicry from target engagement.

- Hypothesis set omitted truth class entirely; over-weighted NSC 3/4 and k-NN 7-8/10 stabilizer votes while dismissing 2/10 Protein degradation proxy and 1/10 Actin at low dose e7 0.651 similarity
- Inflated certainty 0.92->0.96 on n=4 monotonic wells with one replicate/dose, no low-dose control, no orthogonal polymerization or protein synthesis assay

Proposed next experiment: As proposed but with proper controls: 1) cell-free tubulin polymerization assay +/- compound vs paclitaxel and destabilizer, 2) cellular acetylated tubulin and phospho-H3 time course, 3) direct protein synthesis readout puromycin incorporation to test 80S inhibition. This would have separated phenotypic mimicry from target engagement.
